title: Keyframes: animate a clip's box, its volume and layers over time

spec.summary: Keyframes let a value change over time: a picture-in-picture clip that slides in from the side and grows, a logo that fades out, a title that flies in and settles, a clip whose sound dips under a voice. Today every clip box, layer and clip volume holds one value for its whole length, so motion is limited to the photo movement presets. 205 lets the user set values at chosen moments (keyframes) and has the preview and the export move smoothly between them, with a choice of how each change eases. It is the base for later work: transitions (206), speed ramps (207), volume ducking (208) and text animations (210).

US-1.text: As a vlogger, I want my face-cam to slide in from the corner and grow when I start talking, so that the video feels edited rather than static.

US-2.text: As a creator, I want a title to fly in, hold and fade out, so that my Reel opens like the ones I see in my feed.

US-3.text: As a YouTuber, I want a B-roll clip's own sound to dip while I speak over it and come back after, so that viewers hear both without a jump.

US-4.text: As an editor, I want to see, move and delete keyframes on the timeline and choose how each change eases, so that I can fine-tune timing without redoing it.

US-5.text: As a keyboard or screen-reader user, I want to add, find, move and remove keyframes without a mouse and hear what changed.

AC-1.text: These values can be animated (Q1): a picture clip's box (X, Y, size, rotation, opacity, corner radius), a video clip's volume, and a layer's X, Y, size, rotation and opacity. Each animated value is a list of keyframes (a time and a value) in time order; a value without keyframes stays as today.

AC-2.text: Between two keyframes the value follows the first one's interpolation (Q3): **Linear**, **Ease in**, **Ease out**, **Ease in and out** (the standard CSS curves `ease-in`, `ease-out`, `ease-in-out`, within 0.001 of the value) or **Hold** (the value stays until the next keyframe). At a keyframe's time the value is exactly the keyframe's; before the first keyframe it is the first one's value, after the last the last one's. Values never leave their property's range (the ranges of 203's transform, layers and volume).

AC-3.text: Keyframe times are measured from the start of their clip or layer (Q2), so moving a clip or layer (drag, ripple, roll, slide, nudge, a change of track) moves its keyframes with it. Trimming a clip's start keeps every keyframe at the same place on the timeline; keyframes that end up outside the clip are kept (an undo or a re-trim brings them back) but don't act. Splitting gives each part the keyframes in its span plus a keyframe at the cut holding the value there, so nothing jumps; duplicating copies them. Slip doesn't move them.

AC-4.text: The project document stores keyframes as optional fields: every existing document opens unchanged and one without keyframes is written back byte-identical. The validator sorts keyframes by time, keeps the last of several at the same time, clamps values to their range, drops non-numeric ones, and enforces at most 100 keyframes per value and 5,000 per project (Q5) with a reason; at least 25 malformed documents never make it throw. A project with keyframes round-trips document → validator → document equal.

AC-5.text: Every edit to keyframes is one undo step: adding, changing a value, moving, deleting, changing an interpolation; a drag (on the stage or on the timeline) is one step however long.

AC-6.text: In the inspector each animatable value has a keyframe button (Q4) that shows whether the value is not animated, has a keyframe at the playhead, or is animated between keyframes. Pressing it starts animating the value with a keyframe at the playhead (or adds / removes the keyframe at the playhead). While a value is animated, changing it at the playhead (its field, a drag on the stage, the arrow keys) adds a keyframe there or updates the one there. Previous / next keyframe buttons move the playhead to the selected clip's or layer's keyframes.

AC-7.text: Under the selected clip or layer the timeline shows a keyframe lane with a diamond per keyframe time (one row per animated value when expanded). A diamond can be selected, dragged in time (snapping to frames, the playhead and the clip's ends, as 202's Snap), deleted with Delete, and given an interpolation from its menu; the diamond's shape shows its interpolation. Keyboard (with the timeline focused): K adds or removes keyframes at the playhead for every animated value of the selection, Alt + [ / Alt + ] go to the previous / next keyframe, and with a keyframe selected ← / → move it a frame (Shift: a second). Each change is announced to screen readers (the value, its time and its new state).

AC-8.text: The preview and the export take every animated value from the same evaluation at each frame's time on the export's frame grid: for a fixture (a clip moving from one corner to the other with Ease in and out while its opacity falls from 100 % to 0 and it turns 90°; a title layer that flies in, holds, and fades), the values at every frame equal the expected list exactly.

AC-9.text: Golden frames: that fixture at 9:16 and 16:9, at 8 sample times including each keyframe's frame, matches its reference within the self-test's tolerance on every GPU backend, the paused preview shows the same frames, and the export renders the same frames from the same inputs.

AC-10.text: Volume keyframes shape a video clip's sound in the export sample by sample (no steps or clicks: within 0.5 dB of the curve) and in the preview within one frame of it; at 0 % the clip is silent. The export's sound sources for a fixture with volume keyframes equal the expected list exactly.

AC-11.text: A project without keyframes is unchanged: pixel-identical preview frames at 10 sample times and identical export inputs (frames, clips, times and sound sources) to 203 for 201's, 202's and 203's fixtures; all existing video e2e tests pass unchanged.

AC-12.text: Working out every animated value for one frame takes at most 0.05 ms (median) for a project with 500 clips and 5,000 keyframes, so keyframes don't slow playback; a project without keyframes does no extra work per frame.

AC-13.text: Everything in AC-6 and AC-7 works from the keyboard; the keyframe buttons, the lane and the interpolation menu have names and states for screen readers; axe finds no serious problems in the inspector and the timeline; at 360 px wide nothing scrolls sideways outside the timeline; with reduced motion the lane and diamonds don't animate.

AC-14.text: `docs/MEDIA-STUDIO.md` (keyframes, interpolations, keys), `specs/lld.md` (the keyframe model, the evaluation, the document fields), `CHANGELOG.md` and the in-app docs (keys) describe the change.

Q1.text: Which values can be animated in 205? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-12):_ a picture clip's box (X, Y, size, rotation, opacity, corner radius, from 203), a video clip's volume, and a layer's X, Y, size, rotation and opacity: what motion, picture-in-picture and titles need. Not in 205: colour adjustments and masks (the colour work of Phase 3), the music's volume (with ducking in 208), text style (colour, size of the font) and the photo movement presets, which stay as they are (Q7).

Q2.text: What are keyframe times measured from? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-12):_ the clip's (or layer's) start on the timeline, so moving it moves its animation. Trimming the start keeps keyframes where they are on the timeline (the motion doesn't jump); keyframes outside the clip are kept but don't act. Slip changes what a video shows, not when its box moves, so it leaves keyframes alone. (The alternative, times in the video's own source, would make a slip move the animation.)

Q3.text: Which interpolations, and which one do new keyframes get? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-12):_ Linear, Ease in, Ease out, Ease in and out, and Hold; a keyframe's interpolation applies to the change that starts at it. New keyframes get **Ease in and out**, which looks natural for motion and fades; the menu changes it. Custom curves (Bézier handles, a graph editor) are out of scope.

Q4.text: How does a user start animating a value? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-12):_ as in most editors, a keyframe button next to each value in the inspector (a diamond: empty when not animated, filled at a keyframe, half when between keyframes). Once a value is animated, any change at the playhead (field, stage drag, arrow keys) sets a keyframe there; to change the whole animation at once the user removes its keyframes (the button's menu: **Remove animation**). The timeline's lane shows and edits the keyframes of the selected clip or layer only, to keep the timeline readable.

Q5.text: Limits? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-12):_ 100 keyframes per value and 5,000 per project, on the web and the desktop app alike: far beyond hand-made animation, and they bound the document and the per-frame work (AC-12).

Q6.text: Agent tools (Constitution XI)? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-12):_ none in 205, as 203 (Q14): keyframes are store actions and pure functions, and the timeline's agent tools, keyframes included, come together in 212.

Q7.text: How do keyframes and a photo's movement preset (zoom in, pan left …) combine? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-12):_ both apply: the preset moves the picture inside its box (as today), keyframes move the box. Turning presets into editable keyframes is left for later; nothing about existing projects changes.

Q8.text: Volume range for keyframes? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-12):_ 0–100 %, the clip volume's range today (no boost above the file's own level); a boost, with a limiter, comes with the audio work in 208.

sections.title: Non-Functional Requirements
sections.markdown:
- **Performance:** keyframes add at most 0.05 ms per frame (AC-12); preview playback and export speed stay within 5 % of 203 for projects without keyframes; no new decoding or memory per keyframe.
- **Accessibility:** every keyframe action works from the keyboard and is announced; names and states for screen readers; reduced motion respected (AC-13).
- **Compatibility:** web and desktop alike; no new dependency; every existing project opens and exports unchanged (AC-4, AC-11).
- **Free and open source:** keyframes are for everyone, on the web and the desktop app.

sections.title: Out of Scope
sections.markdown:
- Keyframes on colour adjustments, looks and masks (Phase 3, the colour work).
- The music's volume, ducking, and boosting a clip above 100 % (208).
- Speed changes and speed ramps (207); transitions (206).
- Text style animation and animation presets (slide, pop, typewriter: 210).
- Custom easing curves, Bézier handles, a graph editor, curved motion paths.
- Agent tools for keyframes (212, Q6).

risks.text: **Audio automation** (§5): overlapping AudioParam events throw, and a curve split across 10 s windows could click. Mitigation: one `setValueCurveAtTime` per source per window and nothing else on that gain node; the curve is a pure function (`gainCurve`, T040) unit-tested for accuracy (±0.5 dB against the exact curve, as `setValueCurveAtTime` interpolates linearly between its points) and for continuity at window joins. The exported sound itself is measured in 290 (AC-10; no self-test spike during the phase, D-033).

**Auto-key surprises** (§6, Q4): once a value is animated, a drag sets a keyframe rather than moving the whole animation. Mitigation: the diamond shows the state everywhere the value is edited, the change is announced with "keyframe at …", and **Remove animation** is one step away.

**Shared layer code with the photo editor** (§4, §8): `drawLayers` and `useLayerPointer` serve both editors. Mitigation: keyframes act only when a time is passed (the video editor); the photo editor's calls don't change and its tests must stay green.

**Start-edge edits** (§3): a missed edit path would make animations jump after a trim. Mitigation: shift keys in the two helpers every start-edge edit uses (`trim` start without ripple, `moveStart`), and a seeded property test (1,000 random edits) that a key's timeline time is kept by start-edge edits and carried by moves.

Decisions and gotchas logged as they come; progress at the end.

sections.title: Approach
sections.markdown:
Keyframes are data on the clip or layer they animate, evaluated by one pure module that the preview, the export,
the stage editing and the inspector all call, so what the user sees is what is exported (Constitution VIII). Under
D-033 every task is proven by unit tests; the e2e, golden-frame and sound checks are listed in 290.

**§1 The model (new `engine/keyframes.ts`, AC-1, AC-2, AC-12).** A keyframe is `{ t, v, ease }`: seconds from the start
of its clip or layer (Q2), the value, and how the change that starts at it eases (Q3). An item's keyframes are a map
from an animatable value to a sorted list: clips animate `x`, `y`, `w`, `rot`, `opacity`, `radius` (203's box) and
`volume`; layers `x`, `y`, `w`, `rot`, `opacity` (Q1). `valueAt(keys, t)` finds the segment by binary search and
interpolates: linear; ease-in / ease-out / ease-in-out as CSS's cubic-bezier curves (0.42, 0, 1, 1), (0, 0, 0.58, 1),
(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1), solved for x by Newton's method with a bisection fallback; hold. Before the first key: the first
value; after the last: the last. `clampValue(prop, v)` keeps values in range (203's `TF_RANGE`, layers', volume 0–1,
Q8). Higher-level helpers: `transformAt(clip, local)` (the clip's `tf` with its animated fields replaced),
`volumeAt(clip, local)`, `layerAt(layer, t)` (the layer with its animated fields at timeline time `t`), and
`isAnimated(item, prop)`. Items without keyframes return their stored values untouched (no allocation per frame).

**§2 Editing keyframes, pure (keyframes.ts, AC-1, AC-5).** `setKey(keys, prop, t, v)` (adds, or replaces the value at a
time within half a frame; new keys get Ease in and out), `removeKey`, `moveKey(prop | all, from, to)` (a key landing on
another replaces it), `setEase`, `animate(item, prop, t)` (the first key, at the current value) and
`stopAnimating(item, prop, t)` (**Remove animation**: the value at `t` becomes the stored one). Limits (Q5): 100 keys
per value, 5,000 per project, refused with a message.

**§3 Keyframes follow their clip (edits.ts, the store, AC-3).** Times are from the item's start, so moves, ripples,
reorders, track changes, nudges and Magnetic packing carry keyframes for free. Only edits that move a start **edge**
shift them, by minus how far the start moved, so they stay at their timeline place: `trim` of a start edge without
ripple, and `moveStart` (the right clip of a Roll, the next clip of a Slide). A ripple start trim keeps the clip's start,
so nothing shifts. Slip never touches them. `splitKeys(keys, at, valuesAtCut)` gives the left part the keys before
`at` plus one at `at` holding the value there, and the right part the keys after `at` shifted by `-at` plus one at 0
(the store's split uses it). Duplicate copies them (the object spread already does). A layer's start edge
(the timeline's layer bar) goes through a new store action `setLayerTimes`, which shifts its keys the same way.

**§4 Drawing (video.ts, layers.ts, AC-8, AC-11).** `renderStack` takes each item's box from `transformAt(clip,
local)` instead of `clip.tf`, so the preview and the export, which both call it, get the same values at every frame.
`drawLayers(ctx, layers, W, H, t)` draws `layerAt(layer, t)` when a time is given (the video editor); the photo editor
passes none and is unchanged. Items without keyframes take the exact code path of today, so 203's projects stay
pixel-identical.

**§5 Sound (timeline.ts audioPlan, videoExport.ts, previewSound.ts, AC-10).** A clip with volume keyframes is in the
sound plan even when its stored volume is 0, and its `SoundSource` carries `gain` (its keys, in clip time). The
export's `mixWindow` then builds one gain curve for the window: the volume curve times the 0.03 s end ramps, sampled
every 5 ms, set with `setValueCurveAtTime` (the only automation on that gain node, so events never overlap); windows
meet exactly, so a curve crossing a 10 s window edge is continuous. The preview's `previewSound` sets each element's
`volume` from `volumeAt` on every sync tick (within one frame). A spike (T001) checks the curve's accuracy (0.5 dB) and
that nothing clicks at window edges before the rest is built.

**§6 Store actions (state/video.ts, AC-5, AC-6).** `toggleKey(item, prop)` (the diamond: animate / add / remove the
key at the playhead), `removeAnimation(item, prop)`, `moveKeys(item, prop | 'all', from, to, key)` (a drag: one undo
step), `setKeyEase(item, prop | 'all', t, ease)`, `deleteKeys(item, prop | 'all', t)`, and two routers that make the
existing editing keyframe-aware: `setClipTransformAt` (used by the stage box, the arrow keys and the inspector's
fields) and `updateLayerAt` (the layers' pointer and fields). A router writes an animated value as a keyframe at the
playhead (Q4: auto-key) and a not-animated one as today. `setClipVolume` does the same for volume. Every action is one
undo step returning its refusal (locked track, a limit).

**§7 Inspector (VideoWorkspace.tsx ClipPanel, LayerPanel's fields, AC-6).** A `KeyframeButton` (a diamond with three
states: not animated, at a key, between keys; `aria-pressed` and a name such as "X: keyframe at 1.20 s") beside each
animatable field: the 203 Position and size fields, the clip's Clip sound slider, and the layers' position, size,
rotation and opacity controls; its menu has **Remove animation**. The fields show the animated value at the playhead.
Previous / next keyframe buttons in each group's heading.

**§8 Stage (useClipTransform.ts, useLayerPointer.ts, VideoWorkspace.tsx).** The stage evaluates before it edits: the
clip box from `transformAt`, the layers passed to `useLayerPointer` as `layerAt(layer, t)`, so hit tests and handles
match what is drawn; their updates go through the §6 routers, so dragging an animated clip or layer sets a keyframe at
the playhead.

**§9 Timeline keyframe lane (Timeline.tsx, new `studio/KeyframeLane.tsx`, AC-7, AC-13).** Under the selected clip's row
(or the selected layer's row) a thin lane shows one diamond per keyframe time (the union of its animated values); an
expand button shows one row per value. A diamond is a button: click selects, drag moves (snapping to frames, the
playhead and the item's ends with 202's `snap`, Alt to skip), Delete removes, its menu (a portal menu like the track
height menu) sets the interpolation; its shape shows it (diamond: ease, square: hold, triangle-ish: linear). Keys with
the timeline focused: K toggles keys at the playhead for every animated value of the selection, Alt + [ / ] jump to the
previous / next key, ← / → (Shift: a second) move the focused diamond. Changes are announced through the timeline's live
region (`describeKeyChange`, timelineRows.ts). Reduced motion: no transitions on diamonds.

**§10 Project document (timeline.ts, layers.ts, AC-4).** `DocClip.keys?` and `Layer.keys?`, written only when present,
so documents without keyframes are byte-identical. The gate (`mergeKeys(raw, props)`) sorts by time, keeps the last of
equal times, clamps values, checks `ease` (unknown → Ease in and out), drops non-finite entries, enforces the limits with
a reason, and never throws; `mergeProject` and `mergeLayers` call it.

**§11 Agent tools.** None in 205 (Q6): 212 adds the timeline's agent tools, keyframes included.

sections.title: Data Structures & Interfaces
Techniques
sections.markdown:
- **Cubic-bezier easing:** x(u) and y(u) for control points (x1, y1, x2, y2); for a progress p find u with x(u) = p by
  Newton's method (8 steps, derivative guard) with bisection fallback, then y(u). Matches the browser's CSS curves to
  1e-4 (unit-tested against sampled `cubic-bezier` values).
- **Binary search** over each value's keys per evaluation: O(log n) per value; a stack of ≤ 8 clips and the layers
  showing at a frame is well under AC-12's 0.05 ms.
- **Gain automation:** `AudioParam.setValueCurveAtTime(curve, start, duration)` with one curve per source per window
  (linear interpolation between 5 ms points: under 0.1 dB from an ease curve), so the mixer's sample-exact gain matches
  the preview's per-tick `volume`.
- **Auto-key routing:** the store, not the components, decides whether a change is a keyframe, so the stage, the arrow
  keys and the fields stay as they are apart from calling the router.

sections.title: Decisions for the maintainer (accepted 2026-10-12: D1–D3 as recommended)
sections.markdown:
- **D1 — The lane's layout.** _Recommended:_ one row of diamonds (every animated value's keyframe times) under the
  selected clip or layer, with an expand button for one row per value. _Alternative:_ always one row per value (clearer,
  but tall: up to 7 rows under a clip).
- **D2 — Keyboard shortcut.** _Recommended:_ **K** toggles keyframes at the playhead for the selection's animated values;
  **Alt + [ / ]** jump between keyframes (Alt avoids the browser's and screen readers' own [ ] shortcuts). _Alternative:_
  no single-key shortcut, only the buttons.
- **D3 — Ease shown on the diamond.** _Recommended:_ the shape shows it (rounded diamond: an ease, square: hold, pointed
  diamond: linear), with the name in its accessible label and tooltip. _Alternative:_ one shape, the ease only in the
  menu and label.

T010.text: Failing tests (`src/engine/keyframes.test.ts`): `valueAt` exact at keys, the first value before and the last after, linear midpoint, `ease-in` / `ease-out` / `ease-in-out` against sampled CSS cubic-bezier values (±0.001), hold; `clampValue` for every property's range (203's box, layers', volume 0–1); `transformAt` / `volumeAt` / `layerAt` replace only animated fields and return the same object when there are no keys; `isAnimated`.

T011.text: Implement plan §1 in `src/engine/keyframes.ts`: `Keyframe`, `Ease`, `ClipKeyProp`, `LayerKeyProp`, `Keyframes`, `valueAt` (binary search; cubic-bezier by Newton with bisection fallback), `clampValue`, `transformAt`, `volumeAt`, `layerAt`, `isAnimated`; `keys?` on `TimedClip` and `LayerBase`.

T012.text: Failing tests (`keyframes.test.ts`): `setKey` (adds; replaces within half a frame; new keys Ease in and out; clamps), `removeKey`, `moveKey` (one value or all at a time; landing on a key replaces it), `setEase`, `animate` / `stopAnimating` (Remove animation keeps the value at the playhead), the limits (100 per value, 5,000 per project, with the message); `shiftKeys`; `splitKeys` (left: keys before the cut + one holding the value at it; right: keys after, shifted, + one at 0).
T012.test: `npx vitest run src/engine/keyframes.test.ts`: the new cases fail

T014.text: Failing tests (`src/engine/timeline.test.ts`, the document gate): ≥ 25 malformed keyframe documents (wrong types, NaN, unsorted, equal times, unknown ease, unknown value names, too many per value and per project, on clips and on layers) never throw and give the expected keys and reasons; a project with keys round-trips document → gate → document equal; 201 / 202 / 203 documents without keys stay byte-identical.
T014.test: `npx vitest run src/engine/timeline.test.ts`: the new cases fail
